tasks.title: Trust record, version 1: the grant and revocation records, their validator and schema, and a pure evaluation that denies by default, lets delegation only narrow, and cascades revocation, as of a stated time
requirements: a trust record has schema 'memev-trust/1' and one of two kinds. A grant names its id, the subject trusted, the issuer, one scope, the purposes it covers (a closed list of two in version 1: contribute and verify), a start, a required expiry after the start, optional evidence references (at most 8, each a text of at most 128 characters) and an optional delegation block { depth (a whole number, 0 or more), parent (a grant id, optional) }. A revocation names its id, the grant it revokes, its issuer, a time and a reason from a closed list (compromised, left, error, other). PROVISIONAL (source: ADR 8 in docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md, which is proposed; full text in docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md, section How trust is granted, scoped, delegated, revoked and audited)

the validator refuses a record with an unknown field, a subject or issuer that is not a subject id of one of the six types of src/engine/identity.mjs, a personal scope (a personal scope is never shared), a scope that validateScope refuses, an empty or unknown purpose, an expiry that is missing or not after the start, evidence over the limits, and a delegation depth that is not a whole number of 0 or more (source: src/engine/identity.mjs:13-14, :66-75; docs/FEDERATION.md:147-151)

evaluate(request { subject, scope, purpose }, { records, roots, at }) returns { eligible, rule, reason, chain } and denies by default: no records, no roots, a grant whose issuer is neither a root nor the holder of a live delegating grant, a purpose or a scope the grant does not name, a time before the start or at or after the expiry, a revoked grant and an invalid request each deny with a rule id. A root is a subject id the caller passes in; there is no default root and no default grant for any subject, device or node. At is required: there is no default to the clock (source: docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md:66-67, deny by default as the safe default of ADR 5, which is not decided; docs/FEDERATION.md:228-230; addendum line 335)

a delegated grant only narrows its parent: the same scope, the same or fewer purposes, an expiry no later than the parent's, and a depth lower than the parent's; a parent of depth 0 cannot delegate. A revocation takes effect from its time, so an evaluation at an earlier time is unchanged, and revoking a grant makes every grant delegated from it ineligible (source: addendum line 274; docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md)

the module is pure: it reads and writes no file, no network and no clock, imports only src/engine/identity.mjs, and does not change its inputs (source: addendum lines 333 to 335, trust is not a store and not access)

out of scope for this task, by design: the choice of any root (roots are a parameter of evaluate and the module has no default root), any grant made automatically or by default for any subject, device or node, any purpose beyond contribute and verify, and any command, route or store that accepts these records; this task defines and tests the record and the evaluation only
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Starts at once: it depends on nothing that is not on main (src/engine/identity.mjs). Defines the trust record and the one function that answers whether a subject is eligible for a purpose in a scope as of a time. It writes nothing, reads no store and has no caller outside its tests: it has no production caller in this task, which is the position SR-1.15 asks to be stated, not a waiver of it. Trust is an eligibility input only: nothing here grants a permission, a membership or a read. The schema file docs/schemas/trust-record-v1.json lists the same fields as the validator. The record format is provisional: a change to it is a new schema version, not an edit of memev-trust/1.

criteria.statement: the validator accepts a grant, a delegated grant and a revocation, and refuses each of these naming the field: an unknown field, a subject id of no known type, a personal scope, a scope with no type, an empty purposes list, a purpose outside contribute and verify, a missing expiry, an expiry not after the start, nine evidence references, a 129-character reference and a negative or fractional delegation depth; the test fails before the module exists and passes after

title: PG-W-21A Trust record v1, its validator and schema, and a pure eligibility evaluation (memev)
request: Programme contract PG-W-21A in memev: the trust record, its validator and schema, and a pure evaluation of eligibility (work package WP21-01). Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. The id is in the style of SO-W-08B: its second part starts with a letter, so the redteam gate's specIdOf reads the whole name and the contract has its own record path; the work package number 21 is not in docs/scope-one/programme/fragments. Why: work breakdown rows 4.3.7 and 4.3.8 are blocked in part because trust governance, the second of the two integrations the addendum names beside the merge boundary, has no definition in this repository. A definition is proposed in ADR 8 (docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md, full text in docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md); this contract builds only its first, self-contained part, the data model and the evaluation, as a library with tests. It is independent of every open pull request: it imports only src/engine/identity.mjs, which is on main, and it reads no store, clock, file or network. The record format is provisional; changing it later is a new schema version. Boundaries: (1) trust is an eligibility input only: nothing here grants a permission, a membership or a read, and a personal scope is never shared. (2) The module has no production caller in this contract: it is a library with tests, and nothing consumes it until a later contract builds on it (PG-W-21B, unsigned, which is not to be signed before the owner signs off ADR 8). (3) crdt-merge stays in its own repository behind the call-out boundary (ADR 6, decided); nothing here touches it. (4) The topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6 stays OPEN and is an input to none of this. Depends on contracts: SO-F-01 (the subject and scope model). Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier. Nothing in this contract decides ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 or SO-A-05, and it adds no role-by-action matrix.
